column5: Sparrows are typical flying songbirds.
Penguins are flightless birds whose wings evolved into flippers.
Ostriches are flightless ratites, too heavy to fly and with reduced wings.
Emus are flightless ratites.
Kiwis are flightless ratites with vestigial wings.
Bats are the only mammals capable of true powered flight.
Bees are winged insects that fly between flowers.
Adult butterflies fly on large wings.
Dogs are wingless land mammals.
Whales are fully aquatic mammals with no means of flight.
Eagles are powerful soaring raptors.
Pigs are wingless land mammals; "pigs might fly" is a byword for the impossible.
Penguins are excellent swimmers that use their flippers underwater.
Ducks are waterfowl that paddle on water with webbed feet.
Fish are aquatic animals that move by swimming.
Whales are aquatic mammals that swim their whole lives.
Dolphins are aquatic mammals and fast swimmers.
Dogs can swim instinctively (the doggy paddle).
Sharks are fish that swim constantly.
A stone is an inanimate object that sinks and cannot move by itself.
A chair is an inanimate artifact with no ability to move by itself.
Dogs are four-legged land mammals that walk.
Snakes have no legs; they slither instead of walking.
Typical fish have fins, not legs, and cannot walk.
Humans walk upright on two legs.
Typical birds walk or hop on their two legs.
Whales have no legs and cannot move on land.
Snails have no legs and crawl on a muscular foot.
A car is a machine that rolls on wheels and has no legs.
Horses are four-legged land mammals that walk.
Humans are the species that uses spoken language.
Dogs bark but have no language or speech.
Lions roar but cannot produce speech.
Cows moo but have no speech.
Monkeys make calls but cannot speak a language.
Trees are living plants.
A stone is inanimate mineral matter.
Bacteria are single-celled living organisms.
A car is a manufactured machine, not an organism.
Dogs are animals that move and act by themselves.
A rock is inanimate matter.
Plants are alive but are not animate in the linguistic and ontological sense because they cannot move by themselves.
A doctor is a person who practises medicine.
A robot is a machine, even if it looks like a person.
A statue is a sculpted object that only depicts a person.
Apples are fruit that people commonly eat.
Rice is a staple grain eaten by people worldwide.
Stones are mineral and cannot be eaten as food.
Hens lay eggs; chickens are egg-laying birds.
The platypus is a monotreme, an egg-laying mammal.
Crocodiles are reptiles that lay eggs in nests.
Dogs are placental mammals that give birth to live young.
Whales are mammals that give birth to live calves.
The cheetah is the fastest land animal (about 100+ km/h).
Sloths are famously slow-moving.
Snails are a byword for slowness.
Unicorns are mythical creatures.
Dragons are legendary creatures (the Komodo dragon is a different concept).
Dogs are real animals.
Mermaids are mythical beings.
In the real world crows cannot produce language.
In Aesop's fables animals such as the crow (The Fox and the Crow) talk.
The fox is a central talking character in Aesop's fables.
Real foxes cannot speak.
In fable convention the fox is the stock cunning trickster.
In The Ant and the Grasshopper the ant stands for hard work.
In fable convention the owl stands for wisdom.
In fables the peacock stands for vanity and pride in its looks.
The wolf talks in Little Red Riding Hood.
Real wolves howl but cannot speak.
Puss in Boots is a talking cat in a fairy tale.
Real cats meow but cannot speak.
The fable layer inherits real-world flight; crows fly in fables too.
The fable layer does not override life; a fable crow is still a living creature.
Fable conventions give animals speech and traits, not flight, so the real-world default holds.
In The Tortoise and the Hare the hare is the fast runner.
In The Tortoise and the Hare the tortoise is slow and wins through persistence.
The wolf talks in Aesop's fables such as The Wolf and the Lamb.
The frog talks to the princess in The Frog Prince.
Real frogs croak but cannot speak.
